newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Breuer-convinced EMU will start on time.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Breuer-convinced EMU will start on time.

text.p: The designated chief executive of Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, said on Tuesday he was convinced that European monetary union will be launched as scheduled on January 1, 1999.
"We are convinced that the euro will come on time," management board member Rolf Breuer, who is due to take over from Hilmar Kopper as chief executive in May, told a news conference.
But he added: "The probability is not 100 percent, there are doubts."

Breuer noted that Germany alone had "in an act of voluntary restraint" committed itself to sticking strictly to the budget deficit criterion which states that a country must keep its budget deficit below three percent of its gross domestic product (GDP).
"I am convinced we're moving in the right direction and that we will reach the intended goal by the intended time on January 1, 1999," Breuer said.
